Light Up a Life is coming back to Magdalen Street, and the tree will be in the window again this year.

Several of you have asked whether we'd be doing it again, and we are. Memory tags are on the counter from Monday 16 November, with a suggested donation of £3. If you'd rather write at home, there are envelopes by the till, and you can bring your tag in whenever suits you.

Seven years this month since my husband Ray died at the hospice. I still remember how hard it was the first time I hung his tag. My hand would hardly do what I asked of it. These days I write his name at the counter, with the same pen, and it has become one of the quieter parts of my week. I'm not telling you that to make this about me. I'm telling you because there's no right way to do this, and whatever you feel when you pick up a tag is all right.

The tree is for anyone who is grieving, not only for families who have been cared for at the hospice. If you have lost someone, you're welcome to write their name. You're also welcome to come in and simply stand by the tree for a while. You don't need to buy anything or say anything. Many people find that being there is enough.

We'll switch the lights on at 4pm on Saturday 28 November. The Gildencroft Primary children are coming back to sing three or four carols, and Doreen has said she is making mince pies again, so bring a warm coat.

Every name on a tag will be read out at the hospice remembrance service on Sunday 13 December at 3pm, in the day centre. You don't have to attend the service for your loved one's name to be read. It's enough that they are remembered here.

Thank you to everyone who came in last year. There were 412 names on that tree, and I was moved by every one of them. Thank you for the carols, the mince pies, the conversations at the counter, and all the kindness you showed us. We couldn't do this without you.

Whether you write a name or just stand a moment by the lights, you are very welcome here.

Jean
